metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 30-day horizons.
- After a price spike (e.g., >45), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: subtract 1–3% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility bias — forecast mean should be anchored to recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overreacts to short-term noise; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to ignore it; apply a “reversion bias” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day below 40.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-cycle corrections — add a 1–2% downward adjustment if true outcome shows 3+ consecutive days above forecast.
- When sentiment is absent, model overestimates upside potential — cap forecast at 10% above recent 14-day high to avoid overconfidence bias.
